question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & -12 \\ -3 & -3 & 36 \end{bmatrix}.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & -12 \\ -3 & -3 & 36 \end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & -12 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y &=-12\\ 0x+0y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x+y=-12.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=-y-12,$ and the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=-y-12\\ y &=y\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}x \\  y \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} -y-12 \\  y \end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=3-3y,$ and the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=3-3y\\ y &=y\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}x \\  y \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 3-3y \\  y \end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Reducing an Augmented Matrix for a Singular 2x2 System to REF and Solving the Resulting System

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 2 & -2 & 4\end{bmatrix}.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce $M$ to row echelon form, and then find the general solution of the linear system represented by the matrix.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Reducing $M$ to echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 2 & -2 & 4\end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-y &=2 \\ 0x+0y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$
x-y=2.
$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=2+y,$ and the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=2+y \\ y &=y\end{aligned}\right.
$$

where $y$ is an arbitrary number. 

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}2+y \\ y\end{bmatrix},\,y\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & -4 \\ 8 & -16 & -32 \end{bmatrix} & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-8){R}_{1} \\  & ∼\begin{bmatrix}1 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}.\end{aligned}
$$

The corresponding system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=-4\\ 0x+0y &=0.\end{aligned}\right.

Since any pair of numbers $x,y$ is a solution of the final equation $0x+0y=0,$ we can remove this equation from the system. So, our system now consists of a single equation

$$

$$

The first variable $(x)$ is the basic variable, and the second variable $(y)$ is the free variable. Solving for the basic variable $(x)$ in terms of the free variable $(y),$ we get $x=2y-4,$ and the general solution is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x &=2y-4\\ y &=y\end{aligned}\right.

In vector form, the general solution can be written as

$$

$$
